I'm fine with the change and by inspection it looks fine, but this should be pretty trivial to test on target, at least to check that it doesn't blow up on boot.

Thanks for looking into my change 👍

Added the manual testing to the commit message.
Overall in support here.
Lets move these into the method and out of the global namespace if the method is the new "right" way.
yep, fixed it 👍
What would you think about adding a few testcases for these new functions?
Done
the 'InPlace' is implied already?  Or did you have more reasoning for wanting that in the name.  Not a big deal either way.
I don't have any preference here. Changed it.
nit: s/illegal/legal/ ?

i thought `[^A-Za-z0-9_]` with `^` symbol means that the match is negated.

So anything not inside that set of characters would match.
 In that case the variable name would be appropriate, right?
yea I missed the ^ somehow.

Why were these two variables swapped?  It's making this patch kind of hard to review.

Now that these are only used in one place, should we remove them from the namespace and put them in the functions themselves?  We don't expect anyone to use these directly after this patch.

> should we remove them from the namespace and put them in the functions themselves?

I pulled these out of the function to avoid possibly repeated construction. 
But we can achieve the same with a `static` local variable. My mistake 😄

Moved them into the functions instead to limit their scope to where they are used 👍
Not sure we need a function with one line.  Just inline these two calls.  The only thing this is deduplicating is the "_". not sure that's worth it here.

> Not sure we need a function with one line.

Changed it to match your preference 👍
In terms of API design, should these be producing a new string?  Functionally they're producing a new string internally, and I don't think we want to lose that.
Fixed it now 👍

I think sanitize is not sufficient enough. Suggestion 'sanitizeForDbusMember' and 'sanitizeForDbusPath'. This will not only show what is sanitized, also why. This gives context in places the functions are used.
Thanks, fixed it 👍

I am also a bit confused about the naming here, as @ed@tanous.net already pointed out o.O

I see `sanitizeForDBusMember` being used to sanitize the last element to append to an object path instead of an actual DBus member.


`sanitizeForDBusPath` does not seem to sanitize object paths, rather dbus members.

This is not related to this patch directly, since you just took over the naming that was already present, but I would like to see them swapped at some point.
As an aside, because we're touching this code, std::regex is famously slow.  These really should be replaced with std::ranges::replace_if, or something of that nature.

Yes, and both of these functions are still wrong, when considering their usage.

- their names are wrong, the 2nd function handles interface names actually
- in the context of their usage, one is directly used to append object path segments, and does not handle empty string
- the lower function (handling interface name segments) also does not handle empty string and ".." cases (not in-spec).

On top of that, their call sites also need patching since some of them rely on plain `std::string` for object path construction.

Thanks for the patch idea, i have prepared something
